title: Living in Wellington, FL: Honest Pros and Cons for 2026
h1: Living in Wellington, FL: The Honest Pros and Cons
seoTitle: Living in Wellington FL: Pros and Cons of Moving to Wellington, Florida
description: Thinking about moving to Wellington, Florida? An honest look at the pros and cons: schools, parks, the equestrian lifestyle, cost of living, traffic, hurricanes and who Wellington is best for.
coverPrompt: Photorealistic golden-hour aerial view of an upscale South Florida suburban neighborhood in Wellington Florida, Mediterranean-style homes with terracotta roofs around a calm lake, palm-lined streets, families biking on a path, lush green landscaping, warm light, no text, no logos

faq.q: Is Wellington, FL a good place to live?
faq.a: Wellington is popular with families for its highly rated schools, parks, safe neighborhoods and community events, and it is world famous for equestrian sports. The main trade-offs are winter season traffic, higher home prices than the county average, HOAs, and a 30 to 45 minute drive to the beach.

faq.q: How far is Wellington, FL from the beach?
faq.a: Wellington is inland in western Palm Beach County. Most residents drive 30 to 45 minutes to reach the beach in Palm Beach or Lake Worth Beach, depending on traffic.

faq.q: What is the population of Wellington, FL?
faq.a: Wellington had 61,637 residents at the 2020 Census.

faq.q: When is traffic worst in Wellington?
faq.a: Traffic is heaviest from January through April, during the equestrian season, especially around South Shore Blvd, Pierson Road, Forest Hill Blvd and State Road 7.

title: Wellington, FL ZIP Codes: 33414, 33449, 33467 and 33411 Explained
seoTitle: Wellington FL ZIP Codes: 33414, 33449, 33467 and 33411 Explained
description: What ZIP code is Wellington, FL? A simple guide to 33414, 33449, 33467 and 33411, which areas each covers, why some Wellington addresses say Lake Worth, and what it means for schools and home searches.
coverPrompt: Photorealistic aerial view of a tidy South Florida suburb in Wellington Florida at midday, winding palm-lined streets, homes around blue lakes and canals, a horse farm with white fences on one side, clear sky, no text, no logos

faq.q: What is the main ZIP code for Wellington, FL?
faq.a: 33414 is the main Wellington ZIP code and covers most of the village, including Town Center, the Mall at Wellington Green area and the equestrian district.

faq.q: What ZIP codes are in Wellington, FL?
faq.a: Wellington is served mainly by 33414, plus parts of 33449, 33467 and 33411.

faq.q: Why does my Wellington address say Lake Worth?
faq.a: Parts of southern Wellington use the 33449 and 33467 ZIP codes, where Lake Worth is a common mailing city name. A Lake Worth mailing address can still be inside the Village of Wellington.

faq.q: Does my ZIP code determine my school in Wellington?
faq.a: No. Public school zones in Palm Beach County are based on your exact address, not your ZIP code. Check your address with the school district's boundary locator.

seoTitle: Best Parks in Wellington FL: Village Park, Peaceful Waters and More

faq.q: What is the biggest park in Wellington, FL?
faq.a: Village Park on Pierson Road is Wellington's largest sports and recreation park, with fields, courts, a gym, walking paths and playgrounds.

faq.q: Where can you see wildlife in Wellington, FL?
faq.a: Peaceful Waters Sanctuary, with its boardwalk over a restored wetland, and the Wellington Environmental Preserve on Flying Cow Ranch Road are the best spots for birds and other wildlife.

faq.q: Are there free events at Wellington parks?
faq.a: Yes. The Wellington Amphitheater at Town Center hosts free concerts, movie nights and food truck events throughout the year.

title: Schools in Wellington, FL: A Parent's Guide to Public, Charter and Private Options
h1: Schools in Wellington, FL: A Parent's Guide to Public, Charter and Private Options
seoTitle: Schools in Wellington FL: Public, Charter and Private School Guide
description: A guide to schools in Wellington, Florida: every public elementary, middle and high school, how zoning and choice programs work, charter and private options, and Florida school choice scholarships.
coverPrompt: Photorealistic sunny morning scene of a modern elementary school campus in suburban South Florida, children with backpacks walking along a palm-lined path to the entrance, parents waving, bright blue sky, warm natural light, no text, no logos

faq.q: What public high schools serve Wellington, FL?
faq.a: Wellington High School on Greenview Shores Blvd and Palm Beach Central High School on Forest Hill Blvd are the two public high schools serving Wellington, along with Somerset Academy Wellington, a charter high school.

faq.q: How do I find out which school my Wellington home is zoned for?
faq.a: Your home address determines your zoned public schools in Palm Beach County. Use the School District of Palm Beach County's school boundary locator to check a specific address.

faq.q: Are there private schools in Wellington, FL?
faq.a: Yes. Wellington has several smaller private schools, and many families also attend larger private schools nearby such as The King's Academy and Berean Christian School in West Palm Beach. Wingrove Academy, a private PreK-12 school, plans to open in Wellington in 2028.

faq.q: Can I get a scholarship for private school in Florida?
faq.a: Florida's school choice program lets every K-12 student apply for a state-funded scholarship that can be used toward private school tuition. Amounts vary and lower-income families get priority.

title: Mall at Wellington Green: What the 620-Apartment Nordstrom Plan Means for Wellington
h1: The Mall at Wellington Green's Empty Nordstrom Could Become 620 Apartments
seoTitle: Mall at Wellington Green Nordstrom Site: 620 Apartments Proposed
description: Bainbridge Companies has proposed replacing the vacant Nordstrom at The Mall at Wellington Green with 620 apartments. Here is the plan, the $36 million sale, traffic and what happens next.
coverPrompt: Photorealistic golden-hour aerial view of an upscale South Florida suburban shopping mall with palm-lined parking lots and three modern seven-story residential buildings rising beside it, lush green landscaping, soft warm light, no text, no logos

faq.q: What is replacing the Nordstrom at The Mall at Wellington Green?
faq.a: Bainbridge Companies has proposed demolishing the vacant Nordstrom and building about 620 apartments, described as three seven-story buildings on roughly 18.4 acres.

faq.q: Has the Nordstrom apartment project been approved?
faq.a: Not yet, based on the latest reporting. The application was filed March 31, 2026 and must go through village staff review, advisory boards and the Wellington Village Council. The property sale also needs court approval.

faq.q: When did the Nordstrom at Wellington Green close?
faq.a: The Nordstrom store at The Mall at Wellington Green closed in 2019 and has been vacant since.

faq.q: Who owns The Mall at Wellington Green?
faq.a: The application lists Spinoso Real Estate Group and TM Wellington Green Mall LP as the property owners of record. Spinoso manages the mall.

title: Wellington Village (Village Landing) at K-Park: What to Expect From Wellington's First Downtown
h1: Wellington Village at K-Park: What to Expect From Village Landing
seoTitle: Wellington Village (Village Landing) at K-Park: What to Expect in 2028
description: Everything we know about Village Landing, the Wellington Village town center at K-Park on State Road 7: restaurants, shops, a Hilton hotel, the timeline, traffic plans and the fall 2028 opening.

faq.q: What is Wellington Village?
faq.a: Wellington Village is the name residents and early news coverage used for the mixed-use town center planned on Wellington's K-Park property at State Road 7 and Stribling Way. The developer, Related Ross, officially named the project Village Landing in May 2026.

faq.q: Where is Village Landing in Wellington, FL?
faq.a: Village Landing is on about 71 acres on the west side of State Road 7, just south of Stribling Way and south of The Mall at Wellington Green, next to The Village Green shopping center.

faq.q: When will Village Landing open?
faq.a: Construction began in 2026 and the town center is expected to open in fall 2028. The Wingrove Academy private school on the same land is targeting August 2028 for its first phase.

faq.q: What will be at Village Landing?
faq.a: The latest plan includes about 220,000 square feet of retail, 100,000 square feet of restaurants, 90,000 square feet of offices, a 180 room Hilton hotel and a central lake with a boardwalk.

faq.q: Will Village Landing have apartments?
faq.a: An earlier plan included about 300 apartments, but Related Ross removed them in a May 2026 revision and replaced them with more restaurant, retail and office space.

title: Wingrove Academy: Everything We Know About Wellington's New Private PreK-12 School
h1: Wingrove Academy: Everything We Know About Wellington's New Private School
seoTitle: Wingrove Academy Wellington FL: Opening Date, Tuition and Scholarships
description: Wingrove Academy is a new private PreK-12 school coming to Wellington's K-Park site in 2028. Here is what we know about the campus, opening date, tuition and scholarships for Wellington residents.

faq.q: When does Wingrove Academy open?
faq.a: Wingrove Academy is targeting August 2028 for the opening of its first phase, with a first high school class reported for 2029.

faq.q: Where is Wingrove Academy located?
faq.a: The school is being built on the back portion of Wellington's K-Park property off Stribling Way, west of State Road 7, next to the Village Landing town center.

faq.q: How much is tuition at Wingrove Academy?
faq.a: Tuition has not been announced yet. Early reports said it is expected to be competitive with other independent schools in Palm Beach County.

faq.q: Does Wingrove Academy offer scholarships for Wellington residents?
faq.a: Yes. ElevateED presented about $10 million in need-based scholarships for roughly 100 Wellington students. Applicants must live in Wellington, meet admission standards and demonstrate financial need.

faq.q: Who is building Wingrove Academy?
faq.a: The school is being developed by ElevateED, founded by Education in Motion co-founder Karen Yung, in partnership with Stephen Ross and Related Ross.
